To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the truncated extremal moment problem for the characteristic function of a polynomial with isolated critical points is solved by the moments of a basis for R[p]/I∇, and the asymptotic expansions of the moments in terms thereof are given by the coefficients of the Laurent expansion of the inverse of the Fourier transform of a basis for the quotient algebra.

the truncated extremal moment problem can be solved in a finite number of steps in terms of generators that are the moments of a basis of the quotient ring R[x1,..., xn]/I∈p and that the coefficients of the expansion of the moments in terms these generators can be computed from the monodromies of the complex critical points of the defining polynomial.

the asymptotics of the moments of the truncated L-moment problem for a polynomial with isolated critical points is governed by the monodromies of the gradient ideal, and that these asymptotics can be expressed in terms of a system of generators that is provided by the gradient ideal.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the asymptotic behavior of solutions to systems of polynomial equations with isolated singularities, and we present a finite algorithm which computes the asymptotic expansion for any moment of the truncated solution, in terms of the monodromies and a finite set of moments.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a polynomial p with isolated critical points, the asymptotics of the moments of the solution of the truncated n-dimensional L-moments problem is given by a finite system of generators, in terms of which one can compute the monodromies, and the asymptotics are given by a finite set of monodromies and a finite system of generating moments.

the asymptotic expansion of the solution of the extremal truncated n-dimensional L-moments problem can be obtained in the form of an infinite power series with coefficients given by finite sums of products of the coefficients in the power series expansion of the polynomial p and of the monodromies of p, in terms of a basis for the ring R[x1, …, xn]/I∆p.

the asymptotics of moments of the solution of the truncated L-moment problem are computable, linearly in the generators of the moment problem, in terms of the monodromies and the coefficients of the generating moments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an algorithm for computing the monodromies of a complex polynomial and its moments, based on the monodromie theory for isolated singularities.
we provide a finite algorithm for computing any moment of the truncated extremality condition of the L-moment problem for complex singularities, and we obtain the asymptotics of the moments.

, in the context above, we have a finite algorithm for computing the coefficients of the (asymptotic) Fourier expansion of the solution to the truncated extremal moment problem, in terms of the moments of the generating set, the coefficients of the polynomial p, and the monodronomy of p, linearly in time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of a single isolated critical point, the monodromic structure of p is the only obstruction to the asymptotics of the moments of the truncated extremum L-moment problem.
the monodromies of the critical points of a polynomial are the only obstruction to computing the asymptotics for the moments of its solution.
the monodromic structure of p can be used as a tool for obtaining information about the asymptotic behaviour of the moments of the solution.
